_comment: All values denominated in W (wage-turns). 1 W = one tradesperson's wage for one turn. These are starting defaults to playtest against (Dial 2 in the reference sheet). Re-tune freely; the engine never hardcodes a price.
_termination_comment: Firing risk mirrors real wrongful-termination: the FIRING PLAYER rolls a d6 (no NPC ever rolls). On a roll ≤ threshold the worker sues (you pay court_fee); a second roll ≤ threshold and they WIN (you also pay award). Threshold by case: cause (theft/poor review) safest, then a no-cause layoff while you still have unallocated work, then PUNITIVE (firing someone who's out sick/injured) the riskiest. A legit layoff (no work, no flag, healthy) draws no roll. A Slick Lawyer YOU play shifts the threshold down (worker never lawyers up); a Unionized town shifts it up — Favor busts the union.
_poach_comment: Poached: a rival lures a worker. You may counter — pay 1/2/3 W and roll; they stay on a d6 ≤ (counter+2), i.e. 1W→1-3, 2W→1-4, 3W→1-5 — else they walk (you still paid). Or let them go free.
_job_sizes_comment: The tailored job ladder (JOB-CARDS-PLAN). A generic j1–j6 card skins to whoever draws it, so every trade sees the identical work — crew = max assignable, equip/tier are start gates, gear_all = every worker needs a tool. Values/work are starting points; tune in the harness.
_npc_jobs_comment: Word-of-mouth jobs (JOB-CARDS-PLAN B2). Dot pays normal and on COMPLETION seeds +3 jobs into your deck; Hettrick & Lundgren pay net-90 (terms 3) and if you DON'T work their job the round you draw it, their bad word pulls 2 jobs from your deck; Chief Boon's job is mandatory (8-turn deadline, 3 work, can't be dropped).
_expansion_comment: Growth is a deferred capital project, not an instant button. You pay insurance + a 50% deposit now, six trade contracts go out to the town (one per trade, the landlord pays contract_value each — your growth puts the whole table to work), you keep operating your OLD shop at its low rent, and next round you pay the balance, the fee CAPITALIZES as a leasehold asset, and you move in (or gain capacity). Can't cover the balance → forfeit the deposit and stay put. Keyed by target: improve = in-place +capacity (BBB-gated); shop/warehouse = relocate up.

civil._comment: Dial 5. The DEFENDANT 'gets away' on roll ≤ threshold. ONE modifier: each Slick Lawyer shifts the threshold by lawyer_shift toward the side that plays it (defender +, accuser −). Clamped to [min_getaway, max_getaway] so it's never a sure thing either way. Two bases: getaway_owed = you're clearly in the wrong (didn't pay for delivered work / dodged a vendor) → 1–2 (33%); getaway_dispute = a genuine botched-job dispute → 1–3 (50%). legal_fee is paid by each party regardless of outcome.

npc_demand._comment: Dial 6. Each turn an NPC payable is dodged, roll d6. A natural 6 offers a settlement (pay settle_fraction to clear) — EVERY round. Otherwise pass on (1 + dodge#)+ to dodge again (2+, 3+, 4+, 5+...); fail → court (resolved with the civil getaway resolver at getaway_owed).
